      <title>Controversial US-backed vaccine trial in African newborns halted</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/21/us-vaccine-trial-african-newborns-hepatitis-b</link>
      <description><p>Hepatitis B study in Guinea-Bissau that was to be funded by CDC and that drew global backlash ‘will not move forward’</p><p>The US-backed hepatitis B vaccine trial in African newborns that drew global backlash was halted, the lead researcher said on Wednesday.</p><p>It was “now clear” that the study “will not move forward in Guinea-Bissau”, Frederik Schaltz-Buchholzer, a Danish researcher, <a href="https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/missed-opportunity-guinea-bissaus-children-why-trial-frederik-wttde/">wrote</a> on LinkedIn, adding, “we were not given the necessary governmental approval.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/21/us-vaccine-trial-african-newborns-hepatitis-b">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Flights to third countries where the detainees have no ties are scheduled as early as Wednesday, relatives detail</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/15/immigration-trump-midterms-reader-q-a">Send us your questions about immigration and the midterms</a></p></li></ul><p>Relatives of gravely ill detainees at two <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/florida">Florida</a> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/usimmigration">immigration</a> jails say authorities are about to deport their loved ones to unknown countries in Africa despite worsening medical conditions.</p><p>Flights are scheduled as early as Wednesday, according to the families and the immigration advocacy group the Workers Circle, which has been monitoring conditions and speaking with detainees inside two <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/ice-us-immigration-and-customs-enforcement">Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)</a> facilities in south Florida.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/21/ice-detention-illness-deportation-florida">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/20/rfk-jr-vaccine-researchers-offices-raided-guinea-bissau</link>
      <description><p>Police seize doses of hepatitis B vaccine from people at center of dispute over research on African newborns</p><p>Controversial vaccine researchers who have been praised by Robert F Kennedy Jr, the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) secretary, had their offices in Guinea-Bissau raided by judicial police, who seized doses of hepatitis B vaccines, officials <a href="https://www.facebook.com/policiajudiciariaguinebissau/posts/pfbid02x8etNUtmPjenMNZA69EHECDBcz6U4VzxTvszdthBmFmJ1aaCMwoT9brgRNYyg1Jbl">said</a> on Facebook.</p><p>The researchers have been at the heart of an ongoing dispute over research on African newborns, supported by $1.6m from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and matched by the Pershing Square Foundation and the Bluebell Foundation for a total of $3.2m.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/20/rfk-jr-vaccine-researchers-offices-raided-guinea-bissau">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>US grants deportation reprieve to migrants from Ukraine and Sudan</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/19/us-migrants-deportation-ukraine-sudan</link>
      <description><p>DHS says migrants ‘retain protections’ after temporary protected status was set to expire on Monday</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/15/immigration-trump-midterms-reader-q-a">Send us your questions about immigration and the midterms</a></p></li></ul><p>More than 100,000 people from Ukraine and Sudan can stay in the United States without immediate risk of deportation, the Department of Homeland Security said, in what amounts to a temporary reprieve after their right to stay in the country was set to expire on Monday.</p><p>Temporary protected status was set to end on Monday for about 101,000 Ukrainians and 1,800 Sudanese. But the DHS said an announcement “will be made at the appropriate time”. Until then, the department said in a written statement, Ukrainians and Sudanese in the US covered by those temporary measures “retain protection”. The department did not indicate how long they could stay or when a final announcement would be made on their status.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/19/us-migrants-deportation-ukraine-sudan">Continue reading...</a></description>

News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 12:53:07 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Focus</category><title>Brazil's sprawling favelas require long-term urban planning solutions</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/focus/20261022-brazil-s-sprawling-favelas-require-long-term-urban-planning-solutions</link><description>
As Brazilians head to the polls on Sunday for the second round of presidential elections, our correspondents take us to the heart of the country's favelas, where residents live in unsanitary conditions. Over the past 40 years, the area occupied by Brazilian favelas has almost tripled in size. They now cover around 460,000 hectares, compared with 53,700 in 1985. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0dc5c6f8-ce10-11f1-979d-3f59e19fd7f8/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-e0525447.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0dc5c6f8-ce10-11f1-979d-3f59e19fd7f8/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-e0525447.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">df972616-cd6d-11f1-ada2-4ff42493b79f</guid><pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 12:31:01 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Marine RESSE</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France reports first human case of Shamonda virus, but says there's no public health risk</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261022-france-reports-first-human-case-of-shamonda-virus-but-says-there-s-no-public-health-risk</link><description>
France has reported the first-ever recorded case of a human contracting the Shamonda livestock virus, which is most commonly found in cattle. Public health authorities stressed that there did not appear to be any health risk to the public, adding that the infection had been "an exceptional case" involving a person with a severely compromised immune system.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c90e21c2-ce00-11f1-9ac6-23d55109f116/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25281484289422.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c90e21c2-ce00-11f1-9ac6-23d55109f116/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25281484289422.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">fe771850-ce0a-11f1-a056-69ef70d39ea0</guid><pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 12:22:56 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c90e21c2-ce00-11f1-9ac6-23d55109f116/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25281484289422.jpg">© François Mori, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Press Review</category><title>Are fresh US-Israeli strikes on Iran in the pipeline?</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/press-review/20261022-are-fresh-us-israeli-strikes-on-iran-in-the-pipeline</link><description>
PRESS REVIEW – Thursday, October 22: The New York Times's sources report plans for fresh strikes on Iran after the US midterm elections. In other news, the French Senate publishes a 30-step proposal for how to "take back control", just days after protests gave way to riots. Also, how software engineers found and patched up bugs in the language that makes up 70 percent of the internet. Finally, the story of a man for whom what happened in Vegas did not stay there.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/85419180-cded-11f1-b616-ab78a7fed2ce/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-bd8a83d8.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/85419180-cded-11f1-b616-ab78a7fed2ce/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-bd8a83d8.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">fcff90e8-cdeb-11f1-82ac-a5297acf9f38</guid><pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 11:32:22 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Antonia KERRIGAN</dc:creator></item><item><title>🔴 Live: France will ban 'illegitimate' protests in coming days, says Macron</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20261022-live-paris-bans-protests-after-violent-unrest-as-macron-takes-swipe-at-trump</link><description></description><guid isPermaLink="false">9b9a4d06-ce05-11f1-9084-79dd107cfa0f</guid><pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 10:44:50 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Tête à tête</category><title>Dalai Lama appointed by China 'is going to be a fake one', exiled former Tibetan leader says</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/t%C3%AAte-%C3%A0-t%C3%AAte/20261022-dalai-lama-appointed-by-china-is-going-to-be-a-fake-one-exiled-former-tibetan-leader-says</link><description>
In an interview with FRANCE 24, exiled former Tibetan leader Lobsang Sangay said any successor to the Dalai Lama appointed by China "is going to be a fake one". He also likened Beijing's ethnic unity law to "an ethnic erasure", said Tibetan concerns had been "downgraded a bit" in US-China talks and accused China of failing to warn of the deadly August floods on the Nepal-Tibet border.

<![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Thu, 22 Oct 2026 12:00:00 +0000 en <![CDATA[ Next Mass Effect game cancelled as EA shuts down legendary sci-fi RPG studio BioWare ]]> The writing was on the wall, but the news still hit us like a truck yesterday. BioWare, the iconic RPG studio behind the Mass Effect and Dragon Age series, is no more. Development on the next Mass Effect has stopped, but EA might not be entirely done with the IP.

Variety reported, backed by EA’s own statement and BioWare’s goodbye on socials, that EA is laying off 3% of its global workforce and closing down BioWare. The shift comes shortly after the company went fully private this summer, with Saudi Arabia and private equity acquiring it alongside all its studios and properties.

A new Mass Effect game — meant to serve as a follow-up to the original trilogy — had been in development since the early 2020s, though progress was slow following severe downsizing after 2024’s Dragon Age: The Veilguard failed to meet EA’s expectations. According to Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier, only around 50 staff remained at the studio, which would’ve needed to go on a hiring spree to complete development of the massive sci-fi RPG.

The first post-shutdown shocker arrived a bit later, with IGN exclusively revealing that Mass Effect isn't entirely dead, as the upcoming live-action TV show based on Mass Effect is still moving forward at Prime Video.

The series started active development at Amazon in late 2024, but it has yet to reach production status. Little is known about the story, but rumors point to it aiming to bridge the gap between the original trilogy and the now-cancelled new game. Despite closing the studio that created it, EA still owns the Mass Effect property.

Variety’s report, which includes more comments from EA’s top brass about the present and future of the publisher, also contains updates on Marvel’s Iron Man (developed at Motive) and Star Wars Jedi 3 (Respawn Entertainment). Both are still coming, and the more surprising news comes in the shape of DICE and Respawn teaming up for a totally new project, believed to be Star Wars Battlefront 3 after days of strong rumors from a number of reputable sources.

Elsewhere, ex-BioWare developers have teamed up at new studios like Archetype and Arcanaut. The former is preparing to ship Mass Effect-inspired action RPG Exodus in 2027, and the latter recently started work on Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic, with original Knights of the Old Republic (and Mass Effect) director Casey Hudson behind the wheel.

Here’s hoping both studios, as well as the recently laid-off developers, can find success in an increasingly hostile industry.

]]> <![CDATA[ NASA giving update about Artemis moon plans on Oct. 23: Watch it live ]]>

NASA will provide an update about its Artemis moon plans on Friday (Oct. 23), and you can watch it live.

The news will come during a press conference at the agency's Kennedy Space Center in Florida, which starts Friday at 2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT). You can watch it live here at Space.com, courtesy of NASA.

"The update will include details about NASA’s Artemis III mission that will send four astronauts to low Earth orbit next year to test critical systems needed for future lunar landings, and how plans to return American astronauts to the moon by 2028 are progressing," NASA officials said in an Oct. 14 media advisory.

Three agency officials will participate in Friday's "Artemis Acceleration" event. They are:

  • NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman
  • NASA Associate Administrator Amit Kshatriya
  • Jeremy Parsons, NASA’s Artemis program manager

NASA is currently gearing up for Artemis III, which is targeted for mid-2027. The mission will test rendezvous and docking technologies between NASA's Orion capsule and one or both of the private spacecraft that NASA picked to be the Artemis program's crewed lunar landers: SpaceX's Starship and Blue Origin's Blue Moon.

After that will come Artemis IV, which will land astronauts near the lunar south pole in early 2028, if all goes to plan. That will be the first crewed moon touchdown since Apollo 17 way back in 1972.

It's unclear which lunar lander will fly on Artemis IV; that depends on how the development of each one progresses and what happens on Artemis III.

And there will be other landings after Artemis IV. NASA plans to establish a moon base via Artemis, and doing so will require a variety of missions, both robotic and crewed.

The agency feels some urgency in this quest, for China has similar goals. It's important that the U.S. wins this new space race, military and political officials have said, so that the nation can establish the norms of responsible behavior on Earth's nearest neighbor.

]]> <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Oct. 21, 2008: India launches its 1st mission to the moon with Chandrayaan-1 ]]>

On Oct. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. The mission was named Chandrayaan-1, and it consisted of both an orbiter and an impactor.

Chandrayaan-1 launched from the Satish Dhawan Space Center on an Indian rocket called the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, or PSLV-XL. (Launch occurred at 8:52 p.m. EDT, though it was about 6:22 a.m. local time at the launch site on Oct. 22.)

It arrived in lunar orbit about three weeks later and dropped off the Moon Impact Probe, which crashed into the moon on Nov. 14. The rest of the Chandrayaan-1 spacecraft stayed in orbit, where it collected and transmitted data from the moon to Earth for about a year. The mission ended abruptly 14 months ahead of its planned end date when scientists lost contact with the probe.

Why it mattered

The Indian Space Research Organisation, or ISRO, had a lot riding on the success of Chandrayaan-1 moon mission, which marked the first-ever deep space mission by the Indian space agency. It was also the first mission to the moon for India, a country that hopes to launch its own crewed spacecraft and build a space station.

Chandrayaan-1 did more than just demonstrate that India's space program was capable of launching missions to the moon; it also returned some amazing science results, like evidence of water ice on the moon.

"In September 2009, scientists published results of data collected by the American M3 instrument which had detected absorption features on the polar regions of the surface of the Moon usually linked to hydroxyl- and/ or water-bearing molecules," NASA said in a mission overview.

The spacecraft carried 11 instruments to study the moon, five of them built by ISRO. The rest were experiments for the European Space Agnecy and NASA.

"In addition to the five Indian instruments, the spacecraft carried scientific equipment from the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, Sweden, and Bulgaria," NASA said.

It took until Nov. 8, 2008 for Chandrayaan-1 to enter lunar orbit, where it stayed until contact was lost in August 2009, most likely due to a power supply failure caused by overheating.

"This was short of the spacecraft’s planned two-year lifetime, although ISRO noted that at least 95% of its mission objectives had been accomplished by then," NASA wrote.

India did not stop at the moon with Chandrayaan-1. In 2019, the country launched the Chandrayaan-2 orbiter, which carried the Vikram lander and Pragyan rover. Chandrayaan-2 reached lunar orbit successfully, but the Vikram landing failed.

The Chandrayaan-3 misson followed in 2023, which successfully landed a new Vikram lander and Pragyan rover near the moon's south pole. India plans to launch the Chandryaan-4 mission to return moon samples to Earth in 2028.

]]> <![CDATA[ Sci-fi legend Alan Dean Foster on his new futuristic adventure 'Lost On Paradise': 'It's paradise until you get there, and then maybe you mess it up' (interview) ]]> Few names in the science fiction literary world carry as much weight and respect as author Alan Dean Foster. His award-winning 55-year career as a grandmaster of the genre continues with his latest novel from Blackstone Publishing, "Lost on Paradise", and we have an exclusive excerpt to share with our readers ahead of its release this week.

Foster famously ghost-wrote the first "Star Wars" novelization for George Lucas in 1976 and "Splinter of the Mind’s Eye" in 1978, which was intended to be a low-budget Star Wars sequel should the space opera not become a hit. He’s been a mainstay for go-to fantastic adventures featuring engaging characters, dynamic plotlines, and imaginative worlds for six decades.

In addition to crafting the screen story for "Star Trek: The Motion Picture," Foster also wrote the novelizations for the first three "Alien" films, Disney's "The Black Hole," John Carpenter's "The Thing," "The Last Starfighter," "Star Trek," "Transformers," "Terminator: Salvation", and many more.

Lost on Paradise by Alan Dean Foster: $19.99
New York Times bestselling author Alan Dean Foster, master of both action and emotion, reveals a world where everything is perfect, but nothing is as it seems…View Deal

The near-future, off-world escapades of "Lost On Paradise" are the latest addition to Foster’s acclaimed bounty of bestselling standalone novels and series, including the popular "Spellsinger" series.

"Earth is crowded, polluted, and dismal," states the novel's synopsis. "Like millions of others, Jonos and Liina scrape by on her poorly paying job and what little money he gets selling items scavenged from rich people’s trash. Like millions of others, Jonos and Liina dream of Paradise.

"Paradise: a beautiful, clean, verdant world where three races live in harmony—at least, according to the videos sent back to Earth. ]]> <![CDATA[ "A great budget lens for astrophotography, the sharpness produced at f/1.8 and f/2.8 is exactly what you want." Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE lens review ]]>
Key specs

Type: Full-frame prime lens

Focal length: 16mm

Maximum aperture: f/1.8

Lens mount: Sony FE, Nikon Z

Weight: 19.4 oz (550 g)

Dimensions: 3.35 x 4.06-in (85.2 x 103 mm)

Filter thread: 77 mm

Release date: May 2023

As you know, prime lenses come in a wide range of sizes and focal lengths, and every once in a while, one comes along and seems to grab you by the scruff of your neck. One such lens is the Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE, which is an impressive and useful lens for astrophotography thanks to its wide-angle field of view and fast maximum aperture.

This lens is one of the wider prime lenses that are available and could be one of the best third-party lenses for astrophotography. With a price of just $464 (£533), this is one of the most cost-effective wide-angle primes, but rather than being a second-rate lens, its build quality and image quality are fantastic. It’s not the best, but it’s undoubtedly a lens you would enjoy.

Image quality is excellent overall, with no need for lens corrections, except for vignette removal when shooting wide open. With near-perfect sharpness and minimal distortion and aberrations straight out of the camera, perhaps the weight of the lens is a small price to pay.

The lens is made up of 15 elements in 12 groups and is built like a tank, with an all-metal body. It is pretty heavy, though, weighing in at 19.4 oz (550 g) despite its relatively compact size. Attach this lens to one of the best Sony cameras and you will have a formidable combination. The 16mm f/1.8 is also available in the Nikon Z-mount.

Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE lens review

Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE: Performance

  • Great image quality
  • Impressively sharp at f/1.8
  • Excellent corner sharpness

With a focal length of 16mm and a maximum aperture of f/1.8, this is clearly a great lens for astrophotography from a technical point of view. The light-gathering capabilities are excellent, to say the least, and during testing it was possible to shoot at a range of ISO levels with a moonless sky. Even ISO 800 was often high enough for a correct exposure.

The image quality produced by the 16mm f/1.8 is great, with excellent levels of sharpness across the frame. What’s most important here is that even corner sharpness is fantastic when wide open at f/1.8. This is the aperture setting where vignetting is at its strongest, but it reduces drastically when you stop down to f/2.8 and is completely gone by the time you stop down to f/4.

Luckily, though, there is a lens profile in Adobe Camera Raw and Adobe Lightroom that completely removes vignetting. There’s also only minimal chromatic aberration and a tiny amount of barrel distortion, which is impressive given the wide field of view produced by the lens.

As mentioned before, sharpness is great wide open and improves incrementally as you stop down up to the sweet spot of the lens, which is f/8. Sharpness drops slightly at f/11, and it’s at f/16 where diffraction begins to soften the image overall. This increases further when you stop down to f/22.

These latter apertures aren’t relevant to astrophotography; the medium ones aren’t either but the sharpness produced at f/1.8 and f/2.8 is exactly what you want.

Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE: Design

  • Weather-sealed build
  • Compact yet heavy
  • Great handling

The 16mm f/1.8 lens is something of an oddity in one respect: it’s both compact and heavy considering its size, although this comes down to its optical construction. The lens weighs 19.4 oz (550 g) with a size of just 3.35 x 4.06 in (85.2 x 103 mm). It does, however, balance well with Sony A-series cameras.

The 16mm f/1.8 is made up of 15 elements in 12 groups, including four ED glass and three aspherical lenses. The optical construction is designed to deliver sharpness, detail and high contrast with minimal distortion. It’s fair to say it achieves these. Of course, you will experience some perspective distortion when tilting the lens up to capture more of the night sky when there are ground elements in the foreground.

Unlike some wide-angle lenses, the front element isn’t bulbous, and it features an HD nano multilayer coating with a water-resistant and antifouling coating. The filter thread is also just 77mm, so you can easily attach screw-in and square filters if you use them for your astrophotography.

The minimum focusing distance of the lens is 10.6 inches (27 cm), which is great for landscape photographers but less important for astrophotographers.

Build quality is impressive thanks to an all-metal body and weather-sealing. This gives the lens a premium look, and it feels robust in the hand. There’s also a useful digital color screen that displays lens information.

When it comes to controls, there are possibly a few more on this lens than you might find on the average prime. There’s a manual focusing ring that’s wide enough for use when wearing gloves, a manual aperture ring that can be set to stepped and stepless operation using a switch on one side of the lens, two customizable Fn buttons and an AF/MF switch.

Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE: Functionality

  • Small color digital screen
  • Customizable Fn buttons
  • 105.6-degree field of view

The Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE is a full-frame lens offering a generous 105.6-degree field of view, allowing you to capture more of the night sky. This lens naturally works with all Sony FE bodies, and if you shoot APS-C, it will give you an equivalent focal length of 24mm. This means if you currently own an APS-C camera but plan to upgrade to full-frame, this lens could comfortably join you on that journey.

As prime lenses go, this one has a few more bells and whistles than most, so there are a few more things to talk about than usual. Focusing is internal, so the front element doesn’t rotate or extend outwards, which is great when using filters.

For astrophotography, manual focus is the only way to go, but this lens also has autofocus for when you’re shooting other subjects. The autofocus isn't the fastest we’ve seen, taking about 0.25 seconds to lock onto subjects when the lens is wide open, or 0.5 seconds when stopped down. This is driven by an SMT stepping motor, which is quiet but audible.

One feature that you don’t see on many lenses is a small color digital screen on the top of the lens. This shows the focus distance, aperture setting and the active Fn control. Is it a gimmick? A bit. Is it useful? Yes. For astrophotography, the screen is definitely useful because it’s illuminated.

As with most Viltrox lenses, there’s also a USB-C port on the lens mount so it can be powered. This allows you to connect the lens to the Viltrox Lens app via Bluetooth to update firmware and customize the Fn buttons and the digital screen’s welcome screen. This makes firmware updates incredibly easy, which is a great feature to have.

Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE: User reviews

In online reviews, users consistently highlight the lens's value and image quality. Build quality comes up time and time again, thanks to the all-metal build.

Many users report that overall, the lens offers much more than you’d expect for the price and even more than some more expensive lenses.

How we tested the Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE

The Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE was tested in combination with the Sony A7R V, which offers an unforgivingly high resolution. The lens was tested at night with a focus on astrophotography, and in daylight to assess sharpness, distortion and general functionality for an all-round approach to testing.

Should you buy the Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE?

Buy it if:

✅ You’re on a budget: The Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE is less expensive than alternative lenses offering the same focal length and maximum aperture.

✅ You want a wide-angle prime: Thanks to its wide field of view, you can capture more of the night sky, while the fast maximum aperture is ideal for astrophotography.

Don't buy it if:

❌ You would like flexibility: If you would like the flexibility of a variable focal length, a zoom lens is the only way to go. They are typically slower than primes, though.

❌ You'd like a wider view: This is a lovely wide lens, but you can get wider options as both primes and zooms.

Since there are only a few alternatives to the Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE, and given that it offers excellent value for money, this is absolutely a lens worth considering if you need a wide-angle prime.

Furthermore, you’ll struggle to find a similar alternative with the same balance of overall build quality and price. Image quality is excellent, even in the corners and edges of the frame when shooting wide open with minimal distortion.

The two customizable Fn buttons and the illuminated color screen that provides useful lens information are extremely helpful when shooting in the dark.

With a price of $464 (£533) and given its build quality, image quality and overall handling, this lens represents excellent value for money. And while it may be a full-frame lens, APS-C users can still enjoy a 24mm equivalent focal length, so it’s a useful lens for astrophotography whichever format you shoot with.

This is a professional-quality lens with a mid-range price tag, and like other Viltrox lenses, you get the lens, a lens hood, front and rear lens caps and a soft lens case in the box.

If this lens isn't for you

The Viltrox AF 35mm f/1.2 LAB FE is a slightly less wide Viltrox lens with a much faster aperture and is part of the company’s flagship LAB series.

The Sony FE 20mm f/1.8 G is a fantastic wide-angle prime offering excellent image quality in a compact and lightweight form factor.

The Sigma 14mm f/1.4 DG DN Art is something of a beast, both in terms of specs and its size. With a 14mm focal length and f/1.4 maximum aperture, it’s perfect for astrophotography.

]]> <![CDATA[ When will SpaceX and Blue Origin fly to the moon? NASA reveals lunar lander timelines (and an Artemis III update) ]]> NASA has revealed new details about its plans to return astronauts to the surface of the moon, outlining a series of upcoming milestones for SpaceX and Blue Origin as both companies race to ready their lunar landers for the agency's Artemis program.

During an Oct. 5 presentation at the Astronautical Congress (IAC) in Antalya, Türkiye, Steve Creech, acting manager of NASA's Human Landing System (HLS) Program, laid out development timelines for both spacecraft, with key demonstrations planned through early 2028 that include orbital refueling and uncrewed lunar landing tests to qualify the vehicles to fly astronauts to the surface of the moon.

A more pressing deadline, however, is NASA's Artemis III mission, which is targeted for the third quarter (Q3) of 2027. Artemis III will launch four astronauts aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft to low Earth orbit (LEO), where they will rendezvous and dock with test versions of both companies' landers for interoperability checkouts. Those demonstrations will help inform NASA's determination about which lander the agency will choose to carry astronauts to the moon's surface on Artemis IV, targeted for early 2028.

SpaceX and Blue Origin were both awarded NASA contracts to develop HLS vehicles — Starship and Blue Moon, respectively — and have spent the past several years refining their respective lunar lander designs and dealing with various delays along the way. In the face of those delays, and in an effort to better structure its mission progression for success, NASA overhauled its Artemis program architecture in February to maintain its goal of landing astronauts on the moon by the end of 2028 and establish a more regular cadence of uncrewed landings in the meantime.

As part of that shakeup, Artemis III, previously the program's first crewed lunar landing mission, was moved up a year and repurposed for the lunar lander vehicle tests the agency is preparing to fly to LEO next year. The program's first moon landing remains scheduled for 2028, but was shifted to the manifest for Artemis IV.

Between now and then, both SpaceX and Blue Origin have more than a dozen test demonstrations and vehicle milestones to achieve, including success during Artemis III and flights afterward. This will all lead up to a key decision NASA must make: Which vehicle will carry out the first crewed landing on the surface of the moon since the Apollo program ended in 1972?

Starship reached for the first time on its most recent test flight, which occurred on Sept. 28 from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas. NASA lists several other important goals for the vehicle to achieve in 2026, including (in the order listed during the IAC presentation) the first return and catch of the rocket's upgraded Version 3 (V3) booster at its launch pad; the first-ever return and catch of a Ship upper stage; the first Starship launch from one of SpaceX's launch pads still under construction on Florida's Space Coast; and, possibly, the first V3 booster reflight.

NASA also expects SpaceX to complete the initial build of the crew cabin for its lunar lander Starship variant. SpaceX released renders of Starship's interior last year, as well as images of the test elevator astronauts are using to train for Starship egress on the lunar surface, but little else has been made public about the progress the company has made on the cabin's design.

Should the cabin's initial build wrap up by the end of the year, as NASA's presentation suggested, SpaceX will use Q1 2027 to complete integration of the systems that Starship will need to communicate with Orion during Artemis III, and deliver a cabin simulator for astronauts to train on leading up to the mission. SpaceX plans to continue Starship test flights through Q2 of next year, complete a landing leg demonstration and begin crew cabin airlock tests.

Blue Origin's lunar lander mockup is ready for NASA Artemis astronaut training

For Artemis III, SpaceX plans to fly one of its existing V3 Starship upper stages, with some slight modifications. Starship and Orion will dock as part of Artemis III but the SpaceX vehicle won't be equipped with a crew cabin for the mission's astronauts to enter. Between the end of this year and the beginning of the next, SpaceX is expected to complete the addition of a docking system and nosecone cover to the Artemis III Starship vehicle, which, NASA documents suggest, has already completed its mechanical fit checks.

Other notches on SpaceX's checklist leading up to Artemis III include the first propellant transfer demonstration with Starship in orbit. As the first-ever launch vehicle and spacecraft designed for full reusability, Starship's fuel constraints require that its tanks be topped off in order to fly beyond LEO. For a moon landing mission, this could mean up to a dozen launches of SpaceX's Starship "tanker" spacecraft to an orbiting fuel depot, which the moon-bound Starship will visit. To pull that off, though, SpaceX has to show it can successfully transfer those cryogenic fuels on orbit, and also store them effectively enough to prevent too much boil-off.

Starship won't require any refueling flights to complete its objectives for Artemis III, but SpaceX is expected to launch its first Starship tanker vehicle within a few months of that mission as it gears up for the Artemis IV moon landing mission. To that end, a launch of an uncrewed Starship lunar lander variant is targeted sometime toward the end of Q3/beginning of Q4, with an uncrewed lunar landing mission carried out before the end of 2027.

Blue Origin, meanwhile, has its own set of milestones to meet as it develops its Blue Moon Mark 2 (MK2) lander — a 52-foot-tall (16 meters) spacecraft powered by three BE-7 engines. Unlike the bare-bones V3 Starship that SpaceX will launch on Artemis III, Blue Origin plans to fly a completed test vehicle, incorporating the crew cabin, partial life-support, flight software and other systems needed to allow astronauts to enter the lander from Orion during their time docked in LEO. Astronauts will be able to enter Blue Moon from Orion to get a feel for the lander in zero-g and test some of its systems.

NASA's timeline shows the company working to complete a series of manufacturing and testing milestones in the last few months of 2026, including continued BE-7 testing and qualification of Blue Moon's BT-7 maneuvering thrusters. The company also faces its Artemis III interim design review and a critical design review for an upcoming landing demonstration mission in 2028.

Blue Origin is also working to restore its pad at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station's Launch Complex-36 (LC-36) to operation and return its New Glenn rocket to flight, following an explosion of the rocket in May that caused extensive damage to the facility. NASA's presentation places that milestone in Q4 2026, a timeline the company has also been very vocal about maintaining. A recent Reuters report, however, suggests that may not happen until early 2027.

By early 2027, the company expects to complete the spacecraft's communications systems and finalize its flight software, with assembly, integration and testing continuing into Q2. Q1 2027 is also when Blue Origin's Blue Moon MK1 lander (a smaller, uncrewed version of its MK2 successor) will launch to the lunar surface as a part of NASA's Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) program of robotic moon missions.

A photo posted by

During Q2 2027, as the Artemis III mission approaches, Blue Origin is expected to complete integration of its test lander with New Glenn and conclude qualification of its BE-7 engine. Throughout next year, the company plans to continue construction and refurbishments at its launch facilities and hopes to have a new launch pad ready to support the upgraded, more powerful New Glenn 9x4 rocket l by the end of Q3. The first flight of that rocket variant is scheduled for Q4 2027, alongside a second MK1 lunar mission and the launch of an uncrewed MK2 demonstration lander.

That spacecraft is expected to attempt its own uncrewed lunar landing in Q1 2028, around the same time Blue Origin has scheduled a third MK1 flight. Like SpaceX, Blue Origin will need to demonstrate that its lander can safely reach the moon's surface,operate there and return to lunar orbit before NASA clears it to carry astronauts on a future Artemis mission.

NASA's overall timeline remains the same as it has been since the February revamp, with Artemis III expected to launch in mid-2027, followed by a crewed lunar landing on Artemis IV in 2028, and possibly another on Artemis V that same year. There may be changes on the horizon, though. NASA will host a press conference on Friday (Oct. 23) with Administrator Jared Isaacman and Associate Administrator Amit Kshatriya, as well as Artemis program director Jeremy Parsons. SpaceX and Blue Origin still face tight schedules to complete their respective uncrewed landing demonstrations before Artemis IV. With SpaceX targeting Q4 2027 and Blue Origin Q1 2028, both are pushing the margins against NASA's hopes to return astronauts to the lunar surface that same year. Which company ultimately gets the green light for that first landing mission will depend on the progress each makes between now and then, and whether their landers can demonstrate the readiness that NASA requires to safely carry astronauts to the surface of the moon and back again.

]]> <![CDATA[ Orionid meteor shower peaks tonight: Here's the best time to spot shooting stars ]]> Don't miss the Orionid meteor shower peak tonight (Oct. 21-22) as tiny shards of Halley's Comet collide with Earth's atmosphere to carve fiery streaks through the Autumn sky! But will the light cast by the waxing gibbous moon spoil the show?

The Orionid meteor shower activity peaks when Earth travels through the densest section of the debris trail left by Comet 1P/Halley. The comet is currently racing back towards the sun ahead of its next visit to the inner solar system in 2061.

Under perfect dark sky conditions 10 to 20 shooting stars could brighten the night sky each hour as the peak unfolds, according to NASA. However, the light cast by the waxing moon — just four days from being full — will likely reduce the number of visible meteors by hiding fainter Orionids from sight.

Orionid shooting stars will appear to travel away from a point of origin, close to the red star Betelgeuse in the constellation Orion, rising above the eastern horizon an hour before midnight for viewers in the U.S.

When and where to see Orionid shooting stars this October

Your best chance at spotting the fast-moving meteors will come in the hours before dawn on Oct. 22, after the moon has set and the radiant approaches its highest point in the night sky. It's best not to stare directly at the radiant, where the glowing meteor trails will be relatively short compared to those left by shooting stars that appear 45-90 degrees away from the bright star Betelgeuse, thanks to an effect known as foreshortening.

Try to travel away from city lights and allow 20-30 minutes for your eyes to adapt to the dark. Always make sure someone knows where you're going if you head somewhere remote to catch the shower and be sure to take a red light to ensure that you can find your way while also preserving your night vision!

Editor's Note: If you would like to share your Orionid shooting star photos with Space.com's readers, then please send your image(s), along with your name, location and comments to spacephotos@space.com.

]]> <![CDATA[ Russian satellite plays 'cat-and-mouse' with a commercial US spacecraft likely used by Ukraine. But why the risky close encounter? ]]> A Russian satellite just took a very close look at an American spacecraft in low Earth orbit.

A few days ago, the snooping satellite Kosmos 2612 rendezvoused with ICEYE-X36, a commercial craft that observes our planet using synthetic aperture radar (SAR).

The close encounter, which occurred between Oct. 15 and Oct. 19, was reported by Marco Langbroek and other satellite trackers, with Langbroek calling it "a worrisome cat-and-mouse game" in orbit. The rendezvous has garnered a lot of attention in space circles, because it was non-consensual and startlingly close; at one point, the two spacecraft may have been separated by just a few meters. What did Russia hope to gain from it?

Not an isolated incident

A worrisome cat-and-mouse-game in Space

Dr, Marco Langbroek, satellite tracker

Before tackling that question, we need to set the stage a bit. For example, it's important to note that inspections aren't unheard of in the final frontier. Russia, the United States and China have all maneuvered satellites into close proximity of other nations' hardware in recent years.

Most of this activity has taken place in geostationary orbit, which lies 22,236 miles (35,786 kilometers) above Earth. At this altitude, orbital velocity matches our planet's rotational speed, allowing spacecraft to "hover" over one patch of Earth continuously. GEO is therefore a popular destination for spy, communications and weather satellites — and for spacecraft designed to shadow and assess them.

Kosmos 2612 is operating in low Earth orbit (LEO), which is part of the reason its activities have created such a stir. Neither China nor the U.S. has conducted an uncooperative rendezvous in LEO, as far as we know. But Russia has, according to Victoria Samson, chief director of space security and stability for the nonprofit Secure World Foundation.

"They've done a few," she told Space.com. "Kosmos 2543 got within about 30 kilometers [19 miles] of USA 245 in January 2020, and then Kosmos 2558 got within about 70 kilometers [43 miles] of USA 326 in August 2022. And they've done repeated approaches to 326."

Kosmos 2612 got much closer to its target than those other inspectors did, of course. And there's another big difference: USA 245 and USA 326 are classified spy satellites managed by the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office, while ICEYE-X36 is a private Earth-observing craft.

Eyes in the sky

There are about 80 ICEYE spacecraft in LEO at the moment. They image our planet using SAR, which can peer through clouds and gather data both day and night. Some of these satellites are operated by ICEYE, a company based in Finland, while others are managed by its American subsidiary, ICEYE US. ICEYE-X36 is one of the latter.

At least some ICEYE satellites provide imagery to Ukraine, which Russia invaded in February 2022 and continues to assault with ground troops and missile and drone attacks. Indeed, ICEYE signed a contract this past January firming up this data-sharing relationship with Ukraine.

"The agreement ensures that the Ministry of Defence continues to receive a high volume of high-resolution satellite imagery through ICEYE's world-leading SAR constellation, supporting the Ukrainian Armed Forces with persistent situational awareness on tactical timelines," ICEYE representatives said in a January statement.

That likely explains Russia's interest in ICEYE satellites, which is extensive and longstanding. For example, Kosmos 2612 launched in April of this year with five other spacecraft. In May, four members of this fleet, including Kosmos 2612, conducted maneuvers to get into a co-planar orbit with ICEYE-X36. Such maneuvers use a lot of fuel and are therefore not performed lightly. (It's unclear if ICEYE-X36 is dedicated to capturing imagery of Ukraine or Russia, but Russia certainly seems to think it is.)

However, we still don't know the purpose of Kosmos 2612's close approach (which is apparently over, at least for now), Samson stressed.

There are a few possibilities. For example, Russia may want to get a better idea of ICEYE satellites' capabilities, and/or figure out what exactly they're studying on Earth below. Or maybe Kosmos 2612 was actively interfering with ICEYE-X36 in some way — messing with its sensors, perhaps, or blocking or intercepting its communications with the ground.

However, Samson leans toward another explanation.

"I think they're getting frustrated," she said of the Russians.

"They've been kind of in a stalemate, particularly for the past six months or so. And so I think it's just more a matter of demonstrating military prowess in a manner that the Ukrainians cannot respond to," she added. "The Ukrainians are just as good, perhaps even better than, the Russians on drones. But when it comes to space stuff, they're not peers, and this is just a way to remind everyone that that's the case."

As Kosmos 2612's activities show, space is becoming an increasingly competitive and contested domain. The U.S. has long held the advantage above Earth, fielding the most capable reconnaissance and communications craft, but Russia and China are challenging that dominance.

This drama is unfolding above our heads now, and it affects everyone on the planet. Samson therefore wishes that governments around the world were more forthcoming about their space activities — for example, that we learned about Kosmos 2612's shenanigans from the U.S .Space Force rather than from private companies and civilians who pore over government tracking data.

"I think it just speaks to the importance of transparency, and sharing information about these sort of things," she said. "As much as you may want to, you cannot keep the existence of satellites classified, because people can see them."

]]> https://www.space.com/space-exploration/satellites/russian-satellite-plays-cat-and-mouse-with-a-commercial-us-satellite-likely-used-by-ukraine-but-why-the-risky-close-encounter mpDZyehN2GzxXpWvN6vXAF Wed, 21 Oct 2026 10:00:00 +0000 Wed, 21 Oct 2026 10:13:04 +0000 false false false

A Russian satellite just took a very close look at an American spacecraft in low Earth orbit.

A few days ago, the snooping satellite Kosmos 2612 rendezvoused with ICEYE-X36, a commercial craft that observes our planet using synthetic aperture radar (SAR).

The close encounter, which occurred between Oct. 15 and Oct. 19, was reported by Marco Langbroek and other satellite trackers, with Langbroek calling it "a worrisome cat-and-mouse game" in orbit. The rendezvous has garnered a lot of attention in space circles, because it was non-consensual and startlingly close; at one point, the two spacecraft may have been separated by just a few meters. What did Russia hope to gain from it?

Not an isolated incident

A worrisome cat-and-mouse-game in Space

Dr, Marco Langbroek, satellite tracker

Before tackling that question, we need to set the stage a bit. For example, it's important to note that inspections aren't unheard of in the final frontier. Russia, the United States and China have all maneuvered satellites into close proximity of other nations' hardware in recent years.

Most of this activity has taken place in geostationary orbit, which lies 22,236 miles (35,786 kilometers) above Earth. At this altitude, orbital velocity matches our planet's rotational speed, allowing spacecraft to "hover" over one patch of Earth continuously. GEO is therefore a popular destination for spy, communications and weather satellites — and for spacecraft designed to shadow and assess them.

Kosmos 2612 is operating in low Earth orbit (LEO), which is part of the reason its activities have created such a stir. Neither China nor the U.S. has conducted an uncooperative rendezvous in LEO, as far as we know. But Russia has, according to Victoria Samson, chief director of space security and stability for the nonprofit Secure World Foundation.

"They've done a few," she told Space.com. "Kosmos 2543 got within about 30 kilometers [19 miles] of USA 245 in January 2020, and then Kosmos 2558 got within about 70 kilometers [43 miles] of USA 326 in August 2022. And they've done repeated approaches to 326."

Kosmos 2612 got much closer to its target than those other inspectors did, of course. And there's another big difference: USA 245 and USA 326 are classified spy satellites managed by the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office, while ICEYE-X36 is a private Earth-observing craft.

Eyes in the sky

There are about 80 ICEYE spacecraft in LEO at the moment. They image our planet using SAR, which can peer through clouds and gather data both day and night. Some of these satellites are operated by ICEYE, a company based in Finland, while others are managed by its American subsidiary, ICEYE US. ICEYE-X36 is one of the latter.

At least some ICEYE satellites provide imagery to Ukraine, which Russia invaded in February 2022 and continues to assault with ground troops and missile and drone attacks. Indeed, ICEYE signed a contract this past January firming up this data-sharing relationship with Ukraine.

"The agreement ensures that the Ministry of Defence continues to receive a high volume of high-resolution satellite imagery through ICEYE's world-leading SAR constellation, supporting the Ukrainian Armed Forces with persistent situational awareness on tactical timelines," ICEYE representatives said in a January statement.

That likely explains Russia's interest in ICEYE satellites, which is extensive and longstanding. For example, Kosmos 2612 launched in April of this year with five other spacecraft. In May, four members of this fleet, including Kosmos 2612, conducted maneuvers to get into a co-planar orbit with ICEYE-X36. Such maneuvers use a lot of fuel and are therefore not performed lightly. (It's unclear if ICEYE-X36 is dedicated to capturing imagery of Ukraine or Russia, but Russia certainly seems to think it is.)

However, we still don't know the purpose of Kosmos 2612's close approach (which is apparently over, at least for now), Samson stressed.

There are a few possibilities. For example, Russia may want to get a better idea of ICEYE satellites' capabilities, and/or figure out what exactly they're studying on Earth below. Or maybe Kosmos 2612 was actively interfering with ICEYE-X36 in some way — messing with its sensors, perhaps, or blocking or intercepting its communications with the ground.

However, Samson leans toward another explanation.

"I think they're getting frustrated," she said of the Russians.

"They've been kind of in a stalemate, particularly for the past six months or so. And so I think it's just more a matter of demonstrating military prowess in a manner that the Ukrainians cannot respond to," she added. "The Ukrainians are just as good, perhaps even better than, the Russians on drones. But when it comes to space stuff, they're not peers, and this is just a way to remind everyone that that's the case."

As Kosmos 2612's activities show, space is becoming an increasingly competitive and contested domain. The U.S. has long held the advantage above Earth, fielding the most capable reconnaissance and communications craft, but Russia and China are challenging that dominance.

This drama is unfolding above our heads now, and it affects everyone on the planet. Samson therefore wishes that governments around the world were more forthcoming about their space activities — for example, that we learned about Kosmos 2612's shenanigans from the U.S .Space Force rather than from private companies and civilians who pore over government tracking data.

"I think it just speaks to the importance of transparency, and sharing information about these sort of things," she said. "As much as you may want to, you cannot keep the existence of satellites classified, because people can see them."

SpaceX will soon notch a huge spaceflight milestone, if all goes according to plan.

The company will try to catch both stages of its Starship megarocket during the vehicle's next test flight, which is targeted for next month, founder and CEO Elon Musk announced during SpaceX's quarter 3 (Q3) earnings call today (Oct. 20).

If SpaceX succeeds, this "will be the first time that an orbital launch vehicle has been fully recovered," Musk said. "The only way that we can extend consciousness beyond Earth on a sustained basis is with a fully reusable orbital launch vehicle. So this is, I think, a profound technology milestone in the history of civilization and consciousness."

Starship is the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built, standing more than 400 feet (122 meters) tall when fully stacked.

As Musk noted, both of its stages — the Super Heavy booster and Ship spacecraft — are designed to be fully and rapidly reusable, a breakthrough that SpaceX thinks will make Mars settlement and other grand exploration feats economically feasible.

Starship's recovery strategy is different than that for SpaceX's Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy rockets, which are partially reusable. (The latter two rockets have expendable upper stages). Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy boosters come back to Earth on landing pads near the launch site or on ships at sea downrange. Super Heavy and Ship, however, will steer themselves directly back to their launch tower, which will capture each vehicle with its "chopstick" arms.

This will allow SpaceX to inspect, refurbish and refly Starship at an accelerated rate, which is a priority for the company: Musk has said he envisions launching Starship more than 10,000 times per year by 2030.

Starship has conducted 14 test flights to date, and SpaceX has pulled off chopstick catches with Super Heavy on three of them. The company has not yet tried to catch Ship, which is a more difficult proposition, as the upper stage travels higher, farther and faster than the booster does.

Still, Musk is confident that SpaceX will pull off a Ship catch on the first try. (He did not give a specific target date for Flight 15, saying only that it was expected next month.)

"I'd say it's more likely than not that this succeeds next flight," he said. "And if not, we have a steady stream of Starship flight attempts through the end of this year, and and then accelerating next year."

Success would mean back-to-back Starship flights with huge milestones. On Flight 14, which occurred on Sept. 28, Ship reached orbit for the first time ever. It also deployed 26 of SpaceX's Starlink Version 3 satellites — the first 26 members of a next-gen broadband constellation in low Earth orbit that will eventually consist of about 100,000 spacecraft.

The Starship Flight 15 preview was something of an aside during today's call. The event primarily served to announce SpaceX's financial performance during Q3, the three-month stretch that ended on Sept. 30.

And that performance was strong, company representatives said. SpaceX recorded revenues of $14.6 billion during Q3, an increase of 161% from the $5.6 billion earned during Q3 of 2025. The company had a net income of $4.4 billion during Q3, $5.5 billion better than the result from the same stretch last year, when SpaceX lost $1.1 billion.

Just $1.8 billion of 2026 Q3 revenue came from SpaceX's launch division. The vast majority was generated by two other segments — connectivity (services provided by its Starlink megaconstellation) and artificial intelligence (or, as the Trump administration has recently rebranded it, "superintelligence").

SpaceX thinks these latter two segments will continue to boom. That's why it's building the infrastructure to support thousands of Starship launches per year — to loft lots of Starlink satellites and AI data centers to Earth orbit. And the company believes that it's positioned to really start raking in the cash, starting as soon as next year.

"In a nutshell, what this implies for SpaceX annual recurring revenue by the end of '27 is somewhere between 500 billion [dollars] and a trillion," Musk said.

 <description>Detektivové ve spolupráci s kriminalisty zadrželi ve středočeských Zásmukách devětačtyřicetiletého muže, který se vydával za léčitele.  <description>Nová koalice se dohodla na složení Rady města Plzně. Počet členů klesne z dosavadních 11 na 9, sedm z nich bylo v radě i v předchozím volebním období.   <item>
   <title>Vyměnila eura a uložila velkou částku. Jak se přišlo na dobrovolnou prostituci</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/ekonomika/cesko-dobrovolna-prostituce-dane-ustavni-soud/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=ekonomika</link>
   <description>Příjmy z dobrovolné prostituce podléhají v Česku zdanění a finanční úřady mohou po poskytovatelích sexuálních služeb požadovat daň z příjmů. Rozhodl o tom Ústavní soud, který odmítl stížnost ženy, jež nechtěla uhradit doměřené daně za roky 2013 a 2014. Senát vedený soudcem Jiřím Přibáněm potvrdil závěry správních soudů, podle nichž příjmy z prostituce představují běžný ekonomický příjem a nejsou od daně osvobozeny.</description>

  <item>
   <title>Vítala migranty, teď ve Francii brání svůj obchod? Jde o lež, realita je jiná</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/evropa/vitala-migranty-ted-ve-francii-brani-svuj-obchod-jde-o-lez-realita-je-jina/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=evropa</link>
   <description>V prostředí českých i mezinárodních sociálních sítí se od konce minulého týdne masově šíří falešný příběh o francouzské „vítačce migrantů“, která prý vždy podporovala masovou migraci a teď ji zachytilo video, jak se bezmocně snaží zabránit migrantům ve vyrabování svého obchodu. K rozšíření tohoto příběhu aktivně přispěli i někteří čeští a slovenští politici. Jde ale o lež. Obchod, který mladá žena na videu brání, není vůbec její. A neexistuje ani důkaz, že by podporovala migraci.</description>
   <pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 06:05:00 +0200</pubDate>
   <guid>https://www.denik.cz/evropa/vitala-migranty-ted-ve-francii-brani-svuj-obchod-jde-o-lez-realita-je-jina/</guid>

   <title>Pohlreich vyrazí na divoký západ. V saloonu v Plzni najde gastronomické sudoku</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/kultura/ano-sefe-zdenek-pohlreich-plzen-acw-saloon/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=kultura</link>
   <description>Steak, který se nedá ukousnout, záhadné vlčí oháňky a kuchyně vybavená domácím sporákem. Zdeněk Pohlreich tentokrát zamíří do plzeňského ACW Saloonu, kde se majitelé snaží oživit atmosféru divokého západu. Přestože je první ochutnávka téměř katastrofální, šéf si místní partu oblíbí. A nakonec pro ni připraví pořádné překvapení.</description>

  <item>
   <title>Přilepšení k důchodu 2000 korun? Senioři si musí počkat ještě několik měsíců</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/ekonomika/cesko-duchod-duchodci-mimoradny-prispevek-kdy-ho-dostanou-seniori-penze/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=ekonomika</link>
   <description>Zatímco o každoroční valorizaci v zákonném rámci mohou rozhodovat sami ministři, mimořádný příspěvek musí projít standardním legislativním procesem. Proto slíbené peníze důchodci neuvidí už v lednové výplatě penze, ale nejdříve s dvouměsíčním zpožděním. Zadlužení státu to zvýší o miliardy korun.</description>
   <pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 04:00:00 +0200</pubDate>
   <guid>https://www.denik.cz/ekonomika/cesko-duchod-duchodci-mimoradny-prispevek-kdy-ho-dostanou-seniori-penze/</guid>

    <media:description>Na mimořádný příspěvek si čeští důchodci budou muset počkat až do března. Proč? Přečtete si článek.</media:description>

    <item>
      <title>V Praze povládnou STAN a SPOLU, další partnery hledají. Piráti nabídku odmítli</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/volby/portlik-hlavacek-stan-spolu-jednani-koalice-praha.A261022_110046_volby_dyn#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>V Praze je nejspíše jasno o složení koalice, která bude na další čtyři roky vládnout. Jistá je spolupráce STAN a SPOLU, přidat se může ještě třetí partner. Podle lídra Starostů Petra Hlaváčka se zastupitelský klub jeho strany přiklonil k této variantě a odmítl tak spojení Starostů s Piráty a Prahou sobě, bez SPOLU. Jednání budou pokračovat v pondělí.</description>
      <pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 12:49:00 GMT</pubDate>
      <category domain="https://www.idnes.cz/volby">Zprávy - Volby</category>
      <comments>https://www.idnes.cz/volby/portlik-hlavacek-stan-spolu-jednani-koalice-praha.A261022_110046_volby_dyn/diskuse</comments>
      <guid isPermaLink="false">A261022_110046_volby_dyn</guid>
      <media:content url="https://1gr.cz/fotky/idnes/26/103/cl6/DYN6d9530e4aa_122904_19223331.jpg" type="image/jpeg" />
      <media:description>V Praze pokračují jednání o složení koalice po volbách. Již potřetí se od voleb setkává vítězné STAN s koalicí SPOLU pro Prahu. (22. října 2026)</media:description>
      <media:credit>MAFRA</media:credit>
      <media:group>
        <media:content url="https://1gr.cz/fotky/idnes/26/103/cl6/DYN6de371406e_122938_12115260.jpg" type="image/jpeg" />
        <media:content url="https://1gr.cz/fotky/idnes/26/103/cl6/DYN6cacc43480_122834_12890550.jpg" type="image/jpeg" />
      </media:group>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>O Přemyslovce je zájem. Do Národního muzea přilákali statisíce návštěvníků</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/vystava-premyslovci-narodni-muzeum.A261022_142542_vytvarne-umeni_sile#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Na výstavu Přemyslovci – panovnická dynastie a její doba se do Národního muzea přišlo podívat 550 000 lidí. Probíhala v historické budově v Praze od konce dubna do poloviny října a návštěvníci si mohli prohlédnout třeba pohřební klenoty Přemysla Otakara II..</description>
      <pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 12:47:00 GMT</pubDate>
      <category domain="https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci">Zprávy - Domácí</category>
      <comments>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/vystava-premyslovci-narodni-muzeum.A261022_142542_vytvarne-umeni_sile/diskuse</comments>
      <guid isPermaLink="false">A261022_142542_vytvarne-umeni_sile</guid>
      <media:content url="https://1gr.cz/fotky/idnes/26/043/cl6/IHA8f59f202ea_151712_44721630.jpg" type="image/jpeg" />
      <media:description>Národní muzeum. Výstava Přemyslovci. Výstava soustřeďuje více než 900 exponátů ze sedmdesáti institucí z Česka i zahraničí a ukazuje vliv této dynastie na české země i Evropu. (23. dubna 2026)</media:description>

      <media:group>
        <media:content url="https://1gr.cz/fotky/idnes/26/043/cl6/IHA8e2b5dfaf9_151650_23062651.jpg" type="image/jpeg" />

      </media:group>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Průšvih pro AfD. Stranu napadli hackeři, zveřejnili statisíce e-mailů</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni/kyberneticky-utok-strana-afd.A261020_141835_zahranicni_ijan#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Německá opoziční Alternativa pro Německo (AfD) se stala terčem kybernetického útoku. Hackeři, jejichž identita je zatím neznámá, údajně ukořistili a zveřejnili 421 000 e-mailů. AfD útok potvrdila, podle ní ale bylo napadeno jen několik málo e-mailových účtů, z nichž některé se léta nepoužívaly.</description>
      <pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 12:47:00 GMT</pubDate>

    <item>
      <title>Bezdomovec pobodal spícího muže, policisté jej obvinili z pokusu o vraždu</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/plzen/zpravy/pobodani-pokus-o-vrazdu-plzen-hlavni-nadrazi-policie.A261021_075517_plzen-zpravy_epkbn#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Kriminalisté obvinili z pokusu o vraždu pětatřicetiletého muže bez domova, který ve středu ráno pobodal druhého bezdomovce spícího na lavičce. Incident se odehrál před budovou hlavního vlakového nádraží v Plzni. Muž je stíhán vazebně.

      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/snemovna-prvni-cteni-navrh-statniho-rozpoctu-2027-schodek-386-miliard.A261022_045658_domaci_kop#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Poslanci znovu jednají o návrhu státního rozpočtu na příští rok se schodkem 386 miliard korun. „Takto to nechtěli ani vaši voliči,“ řekl v rozpravě místopředseda KDU-ČSL Václav Pláteník. Ke hlasování o rozpočtu se poslanci dostanou zřejmě ve čtvrtek večer, či v noci na pátek.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Ve Francii se poprvé nakazil člověk virem Shamonda. Nemoci podlehl</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni/francie-virus-shamonda-pacient-zemrel.A261022_131626_zahranicni_sile#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Francouzské zdravotnické úřady poprvé zaznamenaly virus Shamonda u člověka. Nakažený pacient později zemřel. Hlavní hypotézou je, že pacient se nakazil na východě Francie, kde byl virus na jaře a v létě letošního roku zaznamenán mezi zvířaty. Úřady ale uvedly, že v současnosti nevidí riziko pro širší populaci. </description>

      <title>Za Ševčíkovo hulvátství se omluvila Malá z ANO, Okamura má jeho slova za nevhodná</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/hulvatstvi-sevcika-vuci-kolegyni-chce-resit-opozice-rakusan-i-omezit-alkohol.A261022_111810_domaci_kop#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Opozici pobouřilo chování poslance SPD Miroslava Ševčíka vůči šéfce poslaneckého klubu STAN Michaele Šebelové. Požadovala proto, aby Sněmovna situaci projednala přednostně, ještě před pokračováním debaty o státním rozpočtu. Ševčík ve středu v noci pokřikoval na Šebelovou, ať si vezme menopauzu, když žádala o přestávku na jednání klubu STAN.</description>

      <media:description>Jednání Poslanecké sněmovny. Stavební zákon. Na snímku Taťána Malá (ANO), Miroslav Ševčík (SPD). (10.července 2026)</media:description>

      <description>K požáru dodávky vyjeli ve čtvrtek hasiči do ulice Hornoměcholupská v Praze. Oheň zasáhl i budovu, vedle které vůz stál. Před příjezdem hasičů se v ní nacházelo několik lidí, nikdo se nezranil. </description>

    <item>
      <title>Složitá jednání probíhají v tichosti, uvedl Kreml ke schůzce Putina s Witkoffem</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni/slozita-jednani-probihaji-v-tichosti-uvedl-kreml-ke-schuzce-putina-s-witkoffem.A261022_141320_zahranicni_bro#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Ruský prezident Vladimir Putin zatím neurčil, kdo se za ruskou stranu zúčastní trojstranného vyjednávání s Ukrajinou a Spojenými státy, řekl mluvčí Kremlu Dmitrij Peskov s tím, že do setkání je zatím ještě čas. Na dotaz novinářů, zda by mohl nabídnout podrobnosti ke středeční schůzce Putina s americkým vyjednavačem Stevem Witkoffem, odpověděl, že podobně složitá vyjednávání probíhají v tichosti.</description>
      <pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 12:15:00 GMT</pubDate>
      <category domain="https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni">Zprávy - Zahraničí</category>
      <comments>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni/slozita-jednani-probihaji-v-tichosti-uvedl-kreml-ke-schuzce-putina-s-witkoffem.A261022_141320_zahranicni_bro/diskuse</comments>
      <guid isPermaLink="false">A261022_141320_zahranicni_bro</guid>
      <media:content url="https://1gr.cz/fotky/idnes/26/103/cl6/ONB6b133efd70_28E_CRISIS_PUTIN_WITKOFF.JPG" type="image/jpeg" />
      <media:description>Vladimir Putin (vlevo) v čele ruské delegace jedná s americkým vyslancem Stevem Witkoffem (vpravo) v Konstantinském paláci v Petrohradu. (21. října 2026)</media:description>
      <media:credit>Reuters</media:credit>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Hackeři zaútočili na ČVUT, univerzita odstavila část systémů</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/hackeri-zautocili-na-cvut-univerzita-odstavila-cast-systemu.A261022_135700_domaci_aoc#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>České vysoké učení technické v Praze (ČVUT) čelilo kybernetickému útoku. Univerzita odstavila část systémů, útok se jí podařilo zastavit. Škola pracuje na řešení problému a obnově. Podle školy útok souvisí s celosvětovými pokusy napadat weby využívající programovací jazyk PHP, v němž byly oznámeny kritické bezpečnostní chyby.</description>
      <pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 12:14:00 GMT</pubDate>

<item>
<title>Obří české AI datacentrum bude používat servery vyrobené v Pardubicích a software z Prahy a Brna</title>
<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/obri-ceske-ai-datacentrum-bude-pouzivat-servery-vyrobene-v-pardubicich-a-software-z-prahy-a-brna/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Potenciální česká AI gigafactory, tedy velké evropské datové centrum pro umělou inteligenci, získala silného partnera. České Radiokomunikace (CRA), které gigafactory mají postavit a provozovat, podepsaly memorandum o spolupráci s francouzskou společností Bull. Ta je v současné době v podstatě jediným vět&#353;ím evropským dodavatelem serverů a clusterů pro AI a superpočítače.</description>

</item>
<item>
<title>Budování internetu v ČR se značně zrychlí a zlevní. Kopat se bude už jen jednou, zákon schválil senát</title>
<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/budovani-internetu-v-cr-se-znacne-zrychli-a-zlevni-kopat-se-bude-uz-jen-jednou-zakon-schvalil-senat/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Výrazně rychlej&#353;í a levněj&#353;í stavba internetu v Česku se přiblížila. Senát tento týden beze změn schválil nový zákon o snížení nákladů na stavbu komunikačních sítí, o něhož se dlouhodobě zasazovali tuzem&#353;tí operátoři a provideři. Zákon v září pro&#353;el poslaneckou sněmovnou. Nyní se čeká na podpis prezidentem, tam se ale nepočítá se zádrhely.</description>

<author>redakce@lupa.cz (Lupa.cz: Jan Sedlák)</author>
<pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 07:14:14 GMT</pubDate>

<guid isPermaLink="false">www.lupa.cz-actuality-18683</guid>


</item>
<item>
<title>Češi vylepšili umělou inteligenci od Nvidie. Je méně „žravá“ a zdarma pro všechny</title>
<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/cesi-vylepsili-umelou-inteligenci-od-nvidie-je-mene-zrava-a-zdarma-pro-vsechny/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Čechům se podařilo vylep&#353;it model umělé inteligence od společnosti Nvidia. Startup BottleCap AI, za kterým stojí Tomá&#353; Mikolov a Jaroslav Beck, upravil jazykový model Nemotron. Tato vylep&#353;ená verze spadá do rodiny modelů ThinkingCap, které Če&#353;i postupně zveřejňují. V rámci série ThinkingCap doposud vy&#353;ly dva upravené modely Qwen od Alibaby, jeden nedávno.</description>

<author>redakce@lupa.cz (Lupa.cz: Jan Sedlák)</author>
<pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 06:00:40 GMT</pubDate>

</item>
<item>
<title>Český AI učitel klavíru získal přes 50 milionů. Projekt už dřív podpořil Kyncl z Warner Music nebo Beck z Beat Saberu</title>
<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/cesky-ai-ucitel-klaviru-ziskal-pres-50-milionu-projekt-uz-driv-podporil-kyncl-z-warner-music-nebo-beck-z-beat-saberu/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Český startup ArtMaster získal v investičním kole 2,4 milionu dolarů (přes 50 milionů Kč) na dal&#353;í vývoj svého AI učitele hudby jménem Artie. Je to aplikace, která poslouchá hru uživatele a rovnou mu přizpůsobuje výuku. Dosud do firmy poslali peníze například Robert Kyncl, generální ředitel Warner Music Group, nebo Jaroslav Beck, zakladatel hry Beat Saber, kterou převzala společnost Meta. Teď se mezi nové přidává mimo jiné Eli&#353;ka Vorel z Google DeepMindu, která má pozici projektové manažerky Gemini.</description>

<author>redakce@lupa.cz (Lupa.cz: Iva Brejlová)</author>

 <description>Francouzské protesty proti vysokým životním nákladům přerostly v násilné nepokoje a střety s policií. V některých částech Paříže platí noční zákaz vycházení. „V ulicích bylo okolo 800 tisíc lidí a většina z nich rozhodně nebyla rabující,“ zdůrazňuje v Pro a proti Sára Vidímová, spolupracovnice Deníku Alarm. „Policisté často říkají, že to byla nejbrutálnější akce, do které kdy byli nasazeni,“ namítá student práv působící ve Francii Ondřej Černý.</description>

 <description>Severoatlantická aliance umožní Ukrajině nakupovat zbraně, munici a vojenské vybavení prostřednictvím své centralizované agentury.  <title>Vyváželi stovky tun odpadu z Německa do Česka. Soud poslal jednatele firmy na 4,5 roku do vězení</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/vyvazeli-stovky-tun-odpadu-z-nemecka-do-ceska-soud-poslal-jednatele-firmy-na-45_2610221321_lar</link>
 <description>Na čtyři a půl roku do vězení poslal ve čtvrtek soud v bavorském Weidenu bývalého jednatele odpadové společnosti Roth International kvůli nelegálnímu vyvezení stovek tun odpadu do České republiky. Vinným shledal také českého řidiče kamionu, který se na vyvezení odpadu podílel. Jemu soud uložil podmíněný trest dva roky vězení.</description>

 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/chtely-svrhnout-republiku-za-nasilnymi-nepokoji-ve-francii-byly-ultralevicove_2610221305_lar</link>
 <description>Za sobotními nepokoji stály rozvratné ultralevicové skupiny, které plánovaly svrhnout republiku. Po schůzce zástupců vlády a tajných služeb to ve čtvrtek podle francouzských médií prohlásil francouzský prezident Emmanuel Macron.</description>

<item>
 <title>Izrael zadržel 90 aktivistů, kteří na Západním břehu Jordánu chránili palestinské farmáře při sklizni oliv</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/izrael-zadrzel-90-aktivistu-kteri-na-zapadnim-brehu-jordanu-chranili-palestinske_2610221054_aru</link>
 <description>Palestinskou sklizeň oliv na okupovaném Západním břehu Jordánu provází násilnosti. Útočí na ně židovští osadníci. Chránit zemědělce proto jezdí západní aktivisté. Ve středu tam Izrael zadržel amerického demokratického politika Brada Landera, celkem pak 90 lidí. Americký politik židovského původu kandiduje do Sněmovny reprezentantů a je spojencem newyorského starosty Zohrana Mamdaniho.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/20231028_144849_240607-132413_epo.jpg?itok=l3trWFM8" type="image/jpeg" />

</item>
<item>
 <title>Jednání mezi Putinem a Witkoffem není pro Ukrajinu moc pozitivní. Řešili spíš americko-ruskou agendu</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/jednani-mezi-putinem-a-witkoffem-neni-pro-ukrajinu-moc-pozitivni-resili-spis_2610220835_aru</link>

 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/pavel-rusko-vede-hybridni-operace-proti-nam-vsem-prikladu-za-rok-je-nekolik_2610220815_ako</link>
 <description>Český prezident Petr Pavel je v Berlíně. Ve středu jednal se spolkovým kancléřem Friedrichem Merzem, ve čtvrtek vystoupí na konferenci o evropské bezpečnosti. Za její největší ohrožení považuje Pavel Rusko, jak řekl novinářům.</description>

<item>
 <title>ONLINE: Ukrajina bude moct nakupovat zbraně levněji a rychleji. A to přes agenturu NATO</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/online-ukrajina-bude-moct-nakupovat-zbrane-levneji-a-rychleji-a-pres-agenturu_2610220732_aru</link>
 <description>Severoatlantická aliance (NATO) umožní Ukrajině nakupovat zbraně, munici a vojenské vybavení prostřednictvím své centralizované agentury, napsal ve čtvrtek list Financial Times (FT). Krok podle něj umožní Ukrajině získávat obranné prostředky rychleji a levněji.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/dsc_4584_260514-133147_jar.jpg?itok=h4K9Fxhw" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 07:32:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Novinář: Putin se rozhodl potrestat Armény za jejich demokratickou volbu. Ale byli jsme na to připravení</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/novinar-putin-se-rozhodl-potrestat-armeny-za-jejich-demokratickou-volbu-ale-byli_2610220700_jho</link>
 <description>Necelé tři dekády po Česku měla svou sametovou revoluci také Arménie. Mladá demokracie teď hledá budoucnost v Evropě, jak potvrdily i letošní parlamentní volby. Jerevan ale dál čelí ruskému ekonomickému tlaku a dezinformacím. Jednou z klíčových osob porevolučního vývoje je novinář Arsen Charatjan. „Rusko v informační válce je a bude aktivní. Projeví se to i v evropských volbách,“ říká pro iROZHLAS.cz. Do Prahy přijel na konferenci Fórum 2000.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/mil04968_260604-165111_jva.jpg?itok=4KN6Lque" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 07:00:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Rusko v noci dvakrát zaútočilo na Kyjev. Rakety v metropoli zranily 22 lidí, jeden člověk zemřel</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/online-rusko-v-noci-dvakrat-zautocilo-na-kyjev-rakety-v-metropoli-zranily-sest_2610220618_aru</link>
 <description>Ruské raketové útoky v noci na čtvrtek v Kyjevě zabily jednoho člověka, dalších 22 zranily, oznámila Státní služba pro mimořádné situace (DSNS). Podle starosty Vitalije Klička je kromě jiného poničena část infrastruktury metra na Jižním mostě přes Dněpr. Ukrajina podnikla dronový nálet na Moskvu a její okolí a starosta metropole Sergej Sobjanin uvedl, že protivzdušná obrana sestřelila většinu ze zhruba 630 dronů. Zraněni podle něj byli dva lidé.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-09-30t082840z_1_261001-083723_kvr.JPG?itok=ekRpvTO6" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 06:18:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
